subject: MAP: NovaCare performance gate and streaming TTFT acceptance
messages:
From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@novacare.health>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: NovaCare MAP: performance gating and timelines

Hi Evelyn and Ben,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — Jon and I went through the example flows and we like the streaming behavior. Before we commit to the Dedicated SKU, Legal & ProdOps need a concrete MAP that defines acceptance criteria for performance (TTFT, streaming p50/p95/p99, concurrency), plus an execution timeline we can include in our procurement binder.

High level asks from NovaCare:
- Must demonstrate TTFT p95 <= 450 ms for initial stream token on our production prompt set.
- Concurrency target: 50 simultaneous chat sessions per region while keeping p95 < 600 ms.
- Sustained throughput to support peak: ~120 reqs/sec (avg 800 tokens per minute) during business hours.
- Clear rollback/canary steps if tails spike during pilot.

Can you share your proposed benchmark plan and an initial MAP with milestones and acceptance gates? We have a purchasing deadline of end of month (2028-03-31) so timeline clarity would help.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Kim
Director, Product Operations
NovaCare
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@novacare.health>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 18:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: NovaCare MAP: performance gating and timelines

Sarah — great to hear. Attached is a draft MAP and our proposed benchmark plan. High level summary here so you can surface it in procurement:

MAP Milestones (summary):
1) MAP Draft & Eval Plan (this week) — define prompts, load profiles, and pass/fail gates.
2) Controlled Benchmark (Redwood infra) — run baseline on H100-backed Dedicated pool, measure TTFT streaming p50/p95/p99, throughput, and concurrency resilience.
3) Canary Pilot (customer sandbox / limited traffic) — 2-week pilot in NovaCare VPC with monitoring and automatic fallback.
4) Final Acceptance — sign-off based on agreed pass/fail gates, followed by capacity reservation.

Benchmark plan (proposed acceptance gates):
- TTFT (first stream token) targets: p50 <= 220 ms, p95 <= 450 ms, p99 <= 900 ms
- Sustained request throughput: support 120 reqs/sec for 30 minutes without p95 regressions > 20% above baseline
- Concurrency: maintain p95 < 600 ms at 50 concurrent sessions; test up to 80 concurrency for stress validation
- Streaming continuity: per-token delivery p50/p95 measured separately; no more than 1% dropped frames/stream disconnects under load

Benchmark scenarios and test harness details are in the attached CSV: prompt distribution (short/medium/long), simulated user think-times, and tokenization profile. Markus will run the controlled benchmark tonight and post results.

Proposed timeline to meet your procurement cutoff: run controlled benchmark and deliver results by Thu 2028-03-15 EOD PT; if green, start canary the week of 2028-03-20 and aim for final acceptance before 2028-03-31.

Will follow up with markers for canary rollback and monitoring dashboards.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Lead, Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 02:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Controlled benchmark results (Novacare prompts) — preliminary

Attaching raw CSV and a short log of an observed tail spike. Summary of the controlled run (H100, 8x A100-like workers in Dedicated pool, model quantized fp16):
- Scenario: mixed prompt set (40% short, 40% medium, 20% long), avg response length 180 tokens
- Sustained load test: 120 reqs/sec for 30 minutes

Measured TTFT (first stream token) — controlled baseline:
- p50: 165 ms
- p95: 390 ms
- p99: 880 ms

Streaming per-token latency (delivery after first token):
- per-token p50: 18 ms
- per-token p95: 55 ms

Throughput / concurrency:
- Sustained throughput observed (tokens/sec across pool): 4,800 tok/sec (equivalent to ~133 reqs/sec given avg tokenization)
- Maintained p95 < 600 ms at 64 concurrent sessions during the test window

Notes: there was a brief tail spike at 00:42:13 UTC (attached log kv_cache_spike_20280314.log). Root cause: cold KV cache on one worker after a model variant fallback; spike lasted ~45s and impacted p99. We applied an immediate warming step and re-ran a 10m validation window — no further spikes.

Next steps:
- I recommend we include a small canary that pins KV-warmup hooks for the first 5,000 sessions and an automatic rollback threshold: if p95 exceeds baseline by 30% for 3 consecutive minutes, stop traffic and divert to fallback model variant.
- Packaging of CSV and an executive one-pager (map-draft-novacare-v3.pdf) is attached.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Senior Performance Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@novacare.health>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jon Cooper <jon.cooper@novacare.health>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 07:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Controlled benchmark results (Novacare prompts) — preliminary

Evelyn / Team — thanks for the fast turnaround and detailed numbers. The preliminary numbers look promising and meet our p95 target. A couple of clarifications before we move to canary:
1) Can you confirm the model variant used in the run (exact tag/hash) and whether the quantized path was used in the canary?
2) For the tail spike, we need a short investigation note that we can attach to procurement describing mitigation steps and expected risk during week-1.
3) Can we push the canary start to Mon 2028-03-20 so our SRE lead can be on-site for first-day monitoring?

If you can confirm 1–2 today, we can lock the timeline and update procurement language to reflect the performance gate.

—Sarah
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@novacare.health>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Controlled benchmark results (Novacare prompts) — confirmation and updated timeline

Sarah — short answers below and an updated MAP timeline.

1) Model tag: redwood/gen-13b@2028-02-21-h100-opt. Quantization: fp16 inference path with model-level fp16 kernels; no int8 path used for the controlled run. Canary recommendation: run the same fp16 path to keep parity.
2) Tail spike note (summary for procurement): one-off KV cache cold start on a single worker during a fallback sequence. Impact: 45s window where p99 inflated to ~1.9s. Mitigations: KV warmup hooks, canary traffic ramping, automated rollback threshold (p95 > 30% baseline for 3m) and on-call escalation to Redwood SRE. Detailed log attached.
3) Canary start: agreed Mon 2028-03-20. Proposed canary plan: 72-hour ramp to 10% traffic, keep SRE watch, metrics reviewed daily; if green, expand to 50% for one week then final acceptance.

Updated acceptance gate (final):
- Controlled benchmark must show TTFT p95 <= 450 ms (met: 390 ms)
- Canary must not exceed controlled p95 by > 20% over a 1-hr rolling window
- No more than 2 production-impacting tail incidents during the 14-day pilot

We'll update the MAP PDF and push the DocuSign + procurement note. If that works, Ben will coordinate procurement items and I will schedule the canary run with Markus.

Thanks — we should be able to meet your procurement deadline with this schedule.

—Evelyn
